admission.justification: The packet contrasts competing prose homes with fixed fields/headings and requires one case-insensitive refusal map to keep later authoring from recreating the drift. The choice governs future authoring and consumers, not this leaf’s schedule.

alternatives.option: Provide typed or fixed homes and refuse newly restated section headings and header labels with their canonical field or operation, while grandfathering existing text.
alternatives.reason: The packet contrasts competing prose homes with fixed fields/headings and requires one case-insensitive refusal map to keep later authoring from recreating the drift.

alternatives.option: Continue accepting newly duplicated free-form sections and header notes for statements that already have a typed or fixed home.
alternatives.reason: The surveyed variety of headings and duplicated fields gives the same fact competing homes and prevents consistent drawing; the packet requires refusals rather than ongoing duplication.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A developer-approved home/skeleton contract deliberately removes the corresponding fixed home or makes a particular label a distinct semantic field.

consequences: New aliases belong to the central authored map rather than being guessed independently by consumers.
Old sections and notes can remain editable/removable; this is not permission for a corpus migration.
context: Recurring non-goal, acceptance, design, objective and dependency statements are scattered among competing section headings and header notes.
